title: Effects of Gender-Affirming Surgery on Interoceptive Awareness.
summary:
BACKGROUND: The inability to correctly identify or appraise internal bodily stimuli, interoceptive awareness (IA), has been shown to be reduced in individuals with body-image dissatisfaction and mental health conditions such as depression and PTSD. IA has not been investigated in relation to gender dysphoria in the transgender and gender diverse (TGD) population, and how this may change in relation to gender-affirming procedures. This study aims to assess pre- and postoperative IA in patients who underwent gender-affirming chest surgery using the Multidimensional Assessment of Interoceptive Awareness (MAIA-2), a previously validated survey.
METHODS: The MAIA-2 survey was administered preoperatively and then repeated at 1 week, 1 month, and 3 months postoperatively to patients who underwent gender-affirming chest surgery between December 2021 and April 2023 at a single institution. The survey was administered once more in September 2024 to collect long-term data. A paired-samples t test was used to compare postoperative mean values to preoperative baselines and obtain P-values. Significance was set as P<0.05.
RESULTS: Twenty-three patients completed the 1-week postoperative survey, 18 patients through 1 month, 16 patients through 3 months, and 13 patients filled out the entire survey set with an average long-term follow-up period of 2.10 years postsurgery. For overall IA, there were significant improvements at each survey interval when compared to preoperative scores. There was a significant increase in the trusting subcategory score at 1 week sustained to long-term follow-up, in the not-distracting score at 1 week and 3 months, and in the not-worrying score at 1 month, sustained to long-term follow-up. There was a nonsignificant upward trend in the attention regulation and self-regulation categories.
CONCLUSION: Gender-affirming chest surgery significantly improves IA early in the postoperative period, sustained to long-term follow-up, demonstrating increased mind-body congruity within TGD patients. Our findings add to the growing body of literature on IA, provide new insight into the postoperative experiences of individuals undergoing gender-affirming surgery, and support providers in more effectively advocating for gender-affirming care.
translation:
相关性：是
标题：性别确认手术对内感受觉知的影响
摘要：背景：无法正确识别或评估内部身体刺激，即内感受觉知（IA），已被证明在身体意象不满以及抑郁和创伤后应激障碍等心理健康状况的个体中有所降低。IA尚未在跨性别和性别多元（TGD）人群中与性别焦虑相关的研究中进行探讨，也未考察其如何随性别确认手术而变化。本研究旨在使用先前已验证的调查工具——多维内感受觉知评估量表（MAIA-2），评估接受性别确认胸部手术患者的手术前后IA水平。
方法：对2021年12月至2023年4月期间在单一机构接受性别确认胸部手术的患者，在术前及术后1周、1个月和3个月时分别进行MAIA-2调查，并于2024年9月再次施测以收集长期数据。采用配对样本t检验比较术后均值与术前基线值，并计算P值。显著性水平设定为P<0.05。
结果：23名患者完成了术后1周调查，18名完成至1个月，16名完成至3个月，13名患者完成了整套调查，平均长期随访时间为术后2.10年。就总体IA而言，与术前评分相比，每个调查时间点均出现显著改善。信任子量表评分在术后1周显著升高并持续至长期随访，不分心评分在术后1周和3个月显著升高，不担忧评分在术后1个月显著升高并持续至长期随访。注意调节和自我调节类别的评分呈非显著上升趋势。
结论：性别确认胸部手术在术后早期显著改善了IA，并持续至长期随访，表明TGD患者的身心一致性得到增强。我们的发现丰富了关于IA的现有文献，为接受性别确认手术个体的术后体验提供了新见解，并支持医疗服务提供者更有效地倡导性别确认护理。
关键词：内感受觉知；性别确认手术；性别焦虑；跨性别与性别多元；身心一致性
